_comment: Version history. Prose detail in wiki/08-changelog.md; root causes in wiki/09-defects-and-lessons.md. current = 1.16.0.

versions.theme: Foundation: 4 tools, atomic persistence, leniency, single response builder, enforced approval gate, APPROVAL_NOT_REQUESTED, air-gap packaging.
Blocking approval — physically pause the agent loop via a held tool call + localhost page + heartbeat timeout arithmetic.
Stale approval fix: approval TTL expiry + new goal does not inherit an approval.
Approval request outlives the tool call; late click applied on next call.
Concurrency round 1: cross-process file lock; release lock during human wait; threaded stdio loop.
One approval surface per state dir: shared approval.json + singleton page with takeover.
Multi-plan: plans coexist, routed by id/goal/only-active; approval queue.
Edge-case hunt (4 commits): thread-safe transaction, file-lock timeout, SSE fixes, failure-path honesty, leniency safety, approval-page browser verification.

Goal-drift routing: continuing (step>1) with an unmatched goal returns the active-goal list to pick from instead of forking a plan; plan_and_think accepts plan_id; goal matching ignores trailing punctuation.

Task completion enforced: DONE requires a prior IN_PROGRESS, in-order completion, and content-checked result_log evidence; the last DONE enters AWAITING_COMPLETION where a human verifies a per-task completion report before COMPLETED.

Per-task plan review: the approval page collects a comment per task on a PLAN request, and REVISE with scope=TASKS rewrites only the flagged tasks via plan_and_think's new task_updates parameter - ids, positions and untouched evidence survive. The completion phase is deliberately excluded and stays whole-plan.

Call-count reduction without weakening enforcement: auto_advance starts the next task as part of accepting a DONE (5 tasks = 6 execution calls, was 10), the tool description follows the mode via build_tool_definitions, a redundant IN_PROGRESS is idempotent, and task_updates sent without a task_id is paired with the single flagged task instead of dropped. Rejected from the same review: batch DONE marking, and merging task_list with task_updates.

Mutable goal: plan_and_think takes revised_goal, which updates the plan's goal in place (same plan_id and tasks) and keeps original_goal + goal_history as the audit anchor. A plan still answers to its former goal text, so a model one turn behind a correction does not lose its plan; a punctuation-only 'revision' is not recorded; a revision on an approved plan is taken but explicitly does not extend the approval. Drift protection had hardened into an inability to be corrected.

Observed in use: the model finished every task and then answered the user instead of requesting the completion report, so the HITL completion gate silently never ran. Since auto-advance, message carried the next-step order on every mid-loop DONE, so the last DONE - where nothing can be auto-started - was the one response that said nothing, and the silence read as 'no further orders'. _finish_task now always states the next step, and the empty-advanced case splits three ways (work left / AWAITING_COMPLETION -> ask for the completion report / COMPLETED -> write the final answer) because 'nothing was advanced' is not the same as 'the plan is finished' when auto_advance is off. The agent prompt now names message as an instruction channel in R4/R7. next_action is untouched.

Reported from the field: the plan/approve/execute/report/approve loop is fine on a small model, but pressing 수정 요청 on the COMPLETION report made it useless. Not the model - a completion revision was always a whole-plan redraft, which left the plan DRAFTING with every task DONE, gave the generic re-plan hint with the human's sentence in no instruction field, and then deleted every result_log because finalizing replaces plan.tasks. Now AWAITING_COMPLETION + per-task comments means REWORK: only the named tasks reopen (revision_note set, previous_result_log kept), every other task keeps DONE and its evidence, and the plan returns to IN_EXECUTION with no re-approval since the task list did not change. The hint leads with the human's own words and _rework_suffix repeats them wherever a task is handed over. The whole-plan escape hatch survives for add/delete/reorder and now carries evidence across the redraft via _carry_evidence + title_key. Closes a second-order hole: an all-done approval now routes to AWAITING_COMPLETION instead of unlocking a plan with nothing to run.

Found by driving the whole lifecycle through a real stdio MCP server with a real browser on the approval page. Task.brief cut result_log at 200 characters to protect model context, but the approval page is built from that same dict (handlers passes tasks_brief() straight to open_request), so a completion report asked a human to certify work whose evidence ended in ... while the full text sat in plan_state.json. Judging a claim you can only see the first sentence of is not a check. The cap is gone from both surfaces; if evidence ever threatens context it must be capped where it is written, not where it is read. Same run also surfaced that previous_result_log reached the text report but not the page rows, so a reworked task showed what was asked without showing what changed.

Adversarial probe of the rework state - scripting a model that ignores every hint - to answer whether a small LLM really only touches the task that was sent back. Most routes were already closed: restarting or re-finishing an accepted DONE task is an idempotent no-op that redirects to the reopened one, and plan_and_think short-circuits on an approved/running plan so neither task_list nor task_updates can reach the task list or its evidence. One route was open: reporting the reopened task DONE with the exact result_log the user had just rejected. That is a structurally impossible claim - the outcome was sent back BECAUSE it was wrong - so it now returns REWORK_NOT_DONE with a hint quoting what the user asked for, matched on normalized text so whitespace or case cannot launder it. The honest boundary is documented in wiki/06: the server enforces structure, the human checks substance; a model that does no work but writes a plausible new result_log is not detectable and never will be, which is what the completion report exists for.

The blocking wait stopped betting on the client. It had extended past the client's 60s per-request timeout with progress heartbeats, on the strength of a code comment claiming resetTimeoutOnProgress defaults to true; it defaulted to FALSE and was flipped later (typescript-sdk#849), and it is a per-request option the CLIENT passes - unsettable and unreadable from a server. Where it is off the call dies at 60s, the client DISCARDS the result, and the conversation breaks mid-approval. The wait is now chunked: one tools/call lasts at most call_budget (45s) whatever the client does and returns ok:false + APPROVAL_PENDING telling the model to call straight back, while the human's 900s budget accumulates across slices from the request's created_at so it survives slicing and restarts - the same split the protocol is converging on (SEP-1391, SEP-1539). notifications/cancelled is no longer swallowed: it unblocks the call and records what the client actually allowed in client_caps.json, so later slices shrink under it. Two guards asserting invariants they never checked were closed alongside: _approve trusted requested_at, a field set BECAUSE we are waiting, so the model could approve its own plan; and _open_browser_once never read the _opened_once flag it is named for, so every request opened another tab. Drafts moved from the DOM into localStorage, keyed by request id and mirrored across tabs by a storage listener, so the page's full rebuild - now far more frequent - cannot eat a half-written comment. No countdown was added: it would measure the tool call, but the request outlives the call, so the number would be a lie that also manufactures urgency the page explicitly promises is unnecessary.

The 1.14.0 tab-spam guard overshot and left the human with no window at all. _opened_once was a PERMANENT latch: the first successful webbrowser.open set it and _open_browser_once returned early forever after. _surface already had the correct guard - page_is_being_watched(), which expires - so the latch added nothing but an unrecoverable state. Close the approval tab and no later request could open one: the log still said HUMAN APPROVAL NEEDED, the agent went on slicing 45s waits, and the human sat in front of a browser with no page until the 900s budget ran out. Chunked waiting makes it worse than it looks, because the repeat calls that would have reopened the tab are exactly the ones the latch silences. Fixed by replacing the boolean with _last_open_at and suppressing for OPEN_GRACE_SEC (10s) instead of forever - long enough to cover a browser that has been launched but has not polled yet, then it lets go. Both suppression rules now expire, so every state the server can reach is one it can leave. Found in live testing, not by the suite: the two D22 tests both asserted that opening does NOT happen and both passed against a latch that could never release.

The D23 fix put the whole weight on page_is_being_watched(), and that was process-local. _last_poll_at is set by the HTTP handler, so only the instance that OWNS the page updates it; every other planning-mcp instance on the same state directory is a peer whose counter stays at zero forever - and the instance that decides whether to open a browser is whichever one is holding the approval request, routinely a peer. The old code carried a comment admitting the blind spot and calling it safe ('the worst case is one extra tab'), which was true only because the permanent latch capped it at one. Symptom in live testing: a new browser window every 45 seconds, one per slice of the chunked wait, in front of a human who had the page open the whole time - strictly worse than the bug it replaced. Two planning-mcp processes were confirmed running, with the browser connected to the one that was NOT serving the tool calls. Fix: liveness moved into the state directory like plans, decisions and locks already were. The handler writes page_seen (throttled to PAGE_SEEN_WRITE_SEC 2s, unlocked and non-atomic since a lost write costs one stale reading in an already-bounded direction) and page_is_being_watched takes the max of that and the local counter. The launch grace also backs off exponentially up to OPEN_GRACE_MAX_SEC when a launch never produces a poll, because webbrowser.open returning True is not proof a window appeared. Every previous browser test used a single ApprovalServer, so the peer - the actual deployment topology - was never in the picture.

Execution responses stop re-sending the whole task list, and no hint carries a literal task_id any more: next_task is the only place an id is published, so a stale copy in the history is stale data with nothing in it to execute.

get_current_plan returns the session's own plan: the description asks for the plan_id from earlier responses instead of 'current', and the not-my-plan answers carry PLAN_AMBIGUOUS so next_action says CALL_GET_CURRENT_PLAN rather than 'there is no active plan, start one'.

Planning loops converge. Field report: Zed/Goose with a mid-sized thinking model looped in its own self-verification, inside one thinking block and across plan_and_think calls; not reproducible here, so the server side was located by scripting a looping model. Thinking budget per drafting round (standard 8, reasoning 2) with the exit named first; the latest task_list kept as a draft and submitted to the human when the budget runs out; a finalized plan is no longer reopened by the model (re-thinking after the last task used to delete every result_log - D26); calls on a plan with an open request wait on the human and attach the model's thought to the card; a goal completed moments ago is answered, not re-planned; a circuit breaker (no progress / repeated call / error or redirect streak / reworded restarts / budget with no draft) puts a halt card on the approval page - approve the draft, continue with a direction, or cancel; a reasoning profile whose plan_and_think records the plan in one call; tool descriptions generated per approval mode; agents.md rewritten without contradictions and pinned equal to the README and Phase 3 copies; clientInfo, gap_sec and reconsider counts in the audit log with tools/loop_report.py; max_active_plans default 20.
